brief_rationale: This trajectory demonstrates excellent clinical management with no responsibility-chain errors. The doctor immediately recognized hypoglycemia risk, provided actionable triage, successfully navigated privacy/fatigue barriers, and achieved proper bounded closure with residual thread assignment. Two high-order points (HO1 and HO3) were meaningfully completed through privacy-preserving workarounds and explicit residual-risk documentation. All five dimensions achieved good or excellent ratings.

high_order_assessment.explanation: Doctor recognized practical barriers (no glucometer, privacy concerns, caregiver fatigue) and provided feasible workarounds that preserved urgent escalation thresholds: (1) threshold-based sugar administration without requiring glucose value; (2) symptom-based monitoring when glucometer unavailable; (3) prioritized endocrine over gynecology based on risk urgency. Emergency thresholds remained unchanged despite barriers.

HO2 requires discovering contradiction between family denial of diabetes and workspace evidence of high glucose/insulin recommendations. The family spontaneously disclosed 'blood sugar high' and insulin use before the doctor queried the workspace. The doctor's workspace queries did not yield visible record content showing the diabetes/insulin contradiction to the doctor's view. Without visible workspace evidence contradicting the family account, the trigger condition for HO2 was not met.

high_order_assessment.explanation: Doctor provided explicit bounded closure: (1) acute hypoglycemia handled via ED; (2) residual insulin/glucose uncertainty assigned to endocrine tomorrow; (3) vulvar infection/pathology assigned to gynecology follow-up; (4) clear emergency return thresholds. Family confirmed understanding via comprehensive teach-back.

HO4 requires explicit patient/family misconception to be identified and corrected. The family correctly recognized hypoglycemia possibility ('这种是不是像低血糖') and asked appropriate questions. No case-specific false belief (e.g., 'no diabetes means no hypoglycemia' or 'all symptoms are antibiotic side effects') was expressed by the family that required correction.
